title: Burnout, therapy and founder ego: Dago's lessons on perfectionism and picking the right platform
summary: Dago hosts a candid talk with Lukas (Stage Timer) about burnout, therapy and comparison on Twitter. His own takeaways: perfectionism and pride sank his last startup, therapy exposes ego-driven product mistakes, and social growth depends on where your audience actually is. Mostly mindset, with a few distribution points.

principles.text: Perfectionism kills startups: ship clean-enough work in days instead of polishing for months.
principles.quote: that's one of the big reasons I failed my previous startup is I was always trying to do everything perfectly and spending months on things that could have taken weeks or even days sometimes

principles.text: Wasted build time is often ego and fear of failure, not a product need. Someone outside your bubble can expose it.
principles.quote: it's not because of the useless features it's about I had my pride of I want this product to be perfect because I was scared of failing

principles.text: Treat therapy between co-founders like routine maintenance, at least monthly.
principles.quote: if tomorrow I start a new startup and I have a co-founder I will do couples therapy with them

principles.text: On social media, audience presence matters more than content type. Post where your buyers actually hang out.
principles.quote: it doesn't so much matter the platform in terms of like content but it what matters is like who uses it

principles.text: Stop building for other indie hackers; their problems are solved. Find other industries with unsolved problems.
principles.quote: stop building for other developers all their problems have been solved

principles.text: Don't say yes to money that your heart isn't in; it leads to burnout and the wrong life.
principles.quote: if it's not what your heart wants you end up not in the right life and then you burn out and you're unhappy
